items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: The story is that one night, on Boston Road in the Bronx, Nancy Wilson was singing and these two guys had a little gig for about twenty dollars, and someone from Capitol Records came in and heard them.

ctx.x: Please do, believe me. The Adderley brothers are my heroes. I love them.

Yeah. Well Nat and I, we did Orlando, Florida last year at Disneyland. He and I. Two cornet players, trumpet players. But during one night in Orlando, Florida, these two little kids came up to Erskine, and the place was packed. And these two little kids had their horns. So one of them said, “Could we play some?” Now this is during the bebop days. This is 1950, 1952. And we had Sonny Payne in the band. As a matter of fact, in the fifties the Erskine Hawkins band went out of business. And that was the best that…

bands. The Alabama State Teacher’s College at Montgomery, the Tennessee State at Nashville, and then several other colleges, they’ve always had great bands and great musicians turn out, like Dwike Mitchell and all those guys from Jacksonville, Edward Waters College. But maybe that is because of the fact that there’s not that much work, you know, when you come out of school. If I told you when I was like maybe, before I came up here, I was offered about maybe ten scholarships, not anything other than playing the…
